content: Personal continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices can be utilized for inpatient glucose monitoring when deemed clinically appropriate. However, they should not replace point-of-care (POC) glucose testing, particularly in situations where critical insulin dosing decisions are being made. Alerts generated by CGM devices for hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia can be valuable for patient management, but proper training is necessary to ensure these alerts are interpreted accurately. For patients who use an Automated Insulin Delivery (AID) system at home, it may be appropriate to continue its use during hospitalization, provided it is done under proper supervision. To ensure the safe and effective use of CGM devices in hospital settings, it is crucial to provide adequate training and education to the healthcare staff involved in their implementation and management.
